nodes.name: On Telegram Event
nodes.notes: Native push trigger — telegram calls this workflow the moment the event happens (no polling). Credential: Telegram bot token. Same bot token as the Telegram node (@BotFather → /newbot).

nodes.name: Probe Endpoint A
nodes.notes: GET https://service-a.example.com/healthz — retries 3× with backoff on failure. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: API key / bearer for the target API. Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.

nodes.name: Probe Endpoint B
nodes.notes: GET https://service-b.example.com/healthz — retries 3× with backoff on failure. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: API key / bearer for the target API. Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.

nodes.name: Combine Probe Results
nodes.notes: Rejoins 2 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

nodes.name: All Healthy?
nodes.notes: Two-way gate on ={{ ($json.statusCode || 200) < 400 }}. TRUE continues the happy path, FALSE takes the alternate branch. Watch out: The false branch carries the non-matching items — wire it deliberately rather than leaving it dangling.

nodes.name: Record Uptime Metric
nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'Event Tracker' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Already Alerted? (State Check)
nodes.notes: Cross-execution dedupe: remembers keys it has processed before and drops repeats — the idempotency guard. Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

nodes.name: Page On-Call via Telegram
nodes.notes: Sends a Telegram message to the configured chat — the same bot can also receive replies, so this doubles as a two-way ops channel. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Telegram bot token. Message @BotFather on Telegram → /newbot → copy the token.

nodes.notes: GET https://enrichment.example.com/v2/lookup — retries 3× with backoff on failure. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. nodes.name: Fold In Enrichment Fields
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes enrichedAt, enrichmentSource. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.notes: Serializes items to a CSV binary file.

# Broadcast stakeholders on changes: Google Sheets & Telegram

**Pattern:** Event Notification · **Level:** Advanced · **Trigger:** Webhook

## Overview

Fires when a webhook arrives, and covers escalations work end to end across Google Sheets and Telegram.

It moves through 21 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. On Telegram Event
2. Probe Endpoint A
3. Probe Endpoint B
4. Combine Probe Results
5. All Healthy?
6. Record Uptime Metric
7. Already Alerted? (State Check)
8. Page On-Call via Telegram
9. Enrich with Reference Data
10. Fold In Enrichment Fields
11. Serialize Run Output (CSV)
12. Archive Row Snapshot
13. Load Previous Snapshot
14. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
15. Stamp Completion Time
16. Persist Run Metadata
17. Fingerprint for Idempotency
18. Drop Already-Processed Items
19. Summarize Run Stats
20. Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
21. Send Summary to Telegram

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Telegram → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing escalations work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

On Telegram Event → Probe Endpoint A → Probe Endpoint B → Combine Probe Results → All Healthy? → Record Uptime Metric → Already Alerted? (State Check) → Page On-Call via Telegram → Enrich with Reference Data → Fold In Enrichment Fields → Serialize Run Output (CSV) → Archive Row Snapshot → Load Previous Snapshot → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Google Sheets) → Send Summary to Telegram → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Telegram → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Google Sheets and Telegram aligned by hand for escalations
- Pushing escalations events into Google Sheets and Telegram the moment they land, not on the next poll
- Escalations work where "Probe Endpoint A" is still a manual step before Google Sheets
- Escalations work that only reaches Google Sheets when a webhook arrives, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Google Sheets and Telegram in step for escalations, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Google Sheets or Telegram are skipped, across all 24 nodes of this escalations build
- A failed Google Sheets or Telegram call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 24 nodes in this escalations build
- Branches rejoin before Google Sheets, so a escalations run reports once rather than 24 times
- Every escalations run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Google Sheets

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; Google OAuth2 / service account; Telegram bot token.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

'Already Alerted?' uses cross-execution dedupe specifically so a service that's down for an hour pages on-call once, not on every scheduled probe — alert fatigue is a real failure mode, and this node is the guard against it.

## Practice exercises

Already production-grade — deepen your understanding:

1. Add a third endpoint to probe and watch the Merge node's input count update.
2. Point a probe at a URL that returns 500 and confirm exactly one page fires, not one per scheduled check.
3. Change the alert dedupe key so alerts re-fire daily instead of once per incident.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Telegram bot token**
Same bot token as the Telegram node (@BotFather → /newbot).
_Gotcha:_ A bot supports only one webhook at a time — a second workflow listening on the same bot steals the updates.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your escalations process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Telegram: the bot token is a bearer credential — rotate it if it ever appears in an execution log.

The HTTP node sends a secret: keep it in a header credential, never in the URL — query strings land in proxy and execution logs.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole escalations payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.

The webhook path is unguessable but it is not authentication: add header auth or an IP allow-list before this endpoint is reachable from the internet.
